Claim 4 (Currently Amended): A method of impeding Leishmania transmission in humans comprising administering to a human subject a therapeutically effective amount of a composition comprising:
(a) a fraction or sub-fraction of Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes called Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) derived from __Leishmania chagasi or Leishmania infantum__, and
(b) saponin,
wherein said composition induces production of blocking antibodies in humans at physiologically relevant concentrations that are capable of preventing parasite transmission by sandfly vectors.

Claim 5 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4 wherein said composition is in the form of a blocking vaccine formulation comprising the FML fraction and saponin in a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier.

Claim 6 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4 wherein said composition further comprises suitable pharmacological vehicles for blocking Leishmaniasis transmission in humans.

Claim 7 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4, wherein the Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, amino acids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine, wherein the FML is derived from __Leishmania chagasi or Leishmania infantum__ and is administered at a dose and schedule sufficient to induce blocking antibodies in human subjects at physiologically relevant serum concentrations.
